full_judgment: 7. In the reported case, the case land appertaining to a permanent tenure stood recorded in CS. Khatian No. 214 under Mouza Shahar Dacca, owned by Akshoy Kumar Saha Banik and Rangubala Choudhurani, Akshoy Kumar Saha Banik instituted Title Suit No. 126 of 1946 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dacca for partition and by the decree passed in the suit Akshoy Kumar Saha Banik got one-third ((1/3)) share while Rangubala got the remaining two-tbird ((2/3)) share. One Nafisa Khatun by purchasing the interest of Akshoy Kumar Saha Banik became co-sharer of Rangubala. Rangubala created a lease in respect of the 2/3rd share for 99 years by a registered deed of lease dated 23-12-53 in favour of Ayesha Khatun. Respondent No. 2 Nafisa Khatun sold her interest to respondent No. 1 by registered sale deed dated 18-4-72. Ayesha Khatun also sold her interest to the appellant by a registered sale deed dated 10-9-73. Against this sale respondent No. 1 filed the application for pre-emption. The appellant contested the case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the respondent No. 2 was not a co-sharer in the tenancy, because the land of the tenure was partitioned by the decree in Title suit No. 126 of 1946 between Akshoy Kumar Saha Banik and Rangubala Choudhurani; and that a separate tenancy was created in favour of Ayesha Khatun by Rangubala by granting permanent lease for 99 years reserving for herself annual rent of Taka 1/-; and that Ayesha Khatun paid rent of Taka 1.00 to the lessor Rangubala till the rent receiving interest was acquired by the Government. The learned Subordinate Judge allowed pre-emption against the appellant and the appeal was dismissed. Thereafter the appellant moved the High Court Division in revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and being unsuccessful moved this court and obtained leave from this court to appeal from the judgment of the High Court Division and their Lordships having considered the provision of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act allowed the appeal with costs and the order allowing pre-emption was set aside and thus the application for pre-emption was dismissed.
